title: Re:ZERO Season 4 Final Episode to Air as 45-Minute Extended Special on September 30
content:
Re:ZERO -Starting Life in Another World- Season 4 will conclude with an extended 45-minute final episode (Episode 19) on September 30, 2026. This will be the eight episode of the second cour, which is subtitled The Recapture Arc .

The first part of the anime dominated our Spring 2026 awards , winning a total of 19 awards, while the anime ranked as a close second in the latest weekly ranking after Episode 18. Studio WHITE FOX is animating.

The staff for the 4th season consists of:

• Original Work: Tappei Nagatsuki

• Original Character Design: Shinichiro Otsuka

• Director: Masahiro Shinohara

• Scenario Supervisor: Tappei Nagatsuki

• Series Composition: Masahiro Yokotani

• Character Design / Chief Animation Director: Haruka Sagawa

• Monster Design: Keitaro Chiba

• Prop Design: Goichi Iwahata, Noritaka Suzuki

• Art Setting: Kaoru Aoki (Bihou)

• Art Director: Ryoka Kinoshita (Bihou)

• Color Design: Izumi Sakamoto

• Director of Photography: Miori Miyagi (T2studio)

• 3D Director: Kentaro Ijima (FelixFilm)

• Editor: Hitomi Sudo (REAL-T)

• Music: Kenichiro Suehiro

• Music Production: KADOKAWA

• Sound Director: Jin Aketagawa

• Sound Effects: Yuji Furuya (Swara Production)

• Sound Production: Magic Capsule

• Animation Production: WHITE FOX

The main cast includes:

• Kobayashi Yusuke as Subaru

• Rie Takahashi as Emilia

• Yumi Uchiyama as Puck

• Inori Minase as Rem

• Rie Murakawa as Ram

• Satomi Arai as Beatrice

• Kana Ueda as Anastasia

• Takuya Eguchi as Julius

• Fairouz Ai as Shaula

The first season of the anime aired in 2016, adapting the light novel series by Tappei Nagatsuki and illustrated by Shinichirou Otsuka . The series also announced 10 major projects for its 10th anniversary this year.

title: Netflix Faces New Backlash After Steel Ball Run JoJo Fans Call for Ending Theme Change Due to Dr. Luke Credit
content:
Netflix is facing new backlash following the release of the ending theme for STEEL BALL RUN JoJo’s Bizarre Adventure at the start of the anime’s 2nd and 3rd STAGE, with some fans calling for the song to be replaced after learning that Dr. Luke is credited as its producer.

The ending, “Shinukaikiruka” by Yuki Chiba, debuted with Episode 2 on September 25. The official credits list Chiba as lyricist, Lukasz Gottwald as composer and Dr. Luke as producer. Gottwald and Dr. Luke are the same person. The song was released digitally alongside a creditless ending video.

Initial criticism focused partly on the song itself. JoJo’s Bizarre Adventure has historically used licensed songs from outside Japan for many of its endings, and some viewers had expected STEEL BALL RUN to continue that tradition. The previous songs included:

• Phantom Blood / Battle Tendency “Roundabout” by Yes

• Stardust Crusaders “Walk Like an Egyptian” by The Bangles

• Stardust Crusaders: Battle in Egypt “Last Train Home” by Pat Metheny Group

• Diamond Is Unbreakable “I Want You” by Savage Garden

• Golden Wind “Freek’n You” by Jodeci

• Golden Wind “Modern Crusaders” by Enigma

• Stone Ocean “Distant Dreamer” by Duffy

Fans quickly began posting alternative edits to the new ending, using songs like “A Horse with No Name,” “The Chain” and “Pony.” Fans are again posting hundreds of comments under unrelated posts on Netflix, urging the streamer to change the outro.

The reaction expanded after attention turned to Dr. Luke’s involvement. Kesha accused the producer in 2014 of sexually assaulting her in 2005. Dr. Luke denied the allegation and filed a defamation lawsuit against her. Their lengthy legal dispute ended in a settlement in 2023, with neither side admitting wrongdoing.

That history has led some JoJo viewers to argue that the issue is more than simply disliking the song. Posts on numerous fan communities specifically call for the ending to be changed because of Dr. Luke’s production credit, while others urge fans to make their concerns known to Netflix and Warner Bros. Japan.

The campaign comes only months after Netflix faced another major online backlash over the STEEL BALL RUN JoJo’s Bizarre Adventure release schedule. Following the 47-minute 1st STAGE in March, fans criticized the lack of clarity about when the series would continue. Netflix later confirmed that the anime would return with weekly episodes , while stating that the split-cour and weekly strategy had been the production committee’s original plan.

STEEL BALL RUN JoJo’s Bizarre Adventure previously revealed the opening video and song ahead of the 2ND and 3RD STAGE premiere on September 25 . The anime previously confirmed 11 episodes for stages 2 and 3, along with weekly streaming on Netflix.

The opening theme song is “SPIN” by Kroi, the band which also performed the opening songs for SAKAMOTO DAYS and Liar Game . You can watch it below.

Steel Ball Run is the seventh part of Hirohiko Araki’s legendary JoJo’s Bizarre Adventure manga. Set in late 19th-century America, the story follows former prodigy jockey Johnny Joestar and mysterious outlaw Gyro Zeppeli as they compete in a transcontinental horse race for a massive cash prize. Beneath the surface, however, they face dangerous conspiracies that threaten to take over the competition. The first episode was a 47-minute special covering Stage 1 of the race, and it released on March 19, 2026. You can watch the latest trailer for the anime below.

Also check out the English dub version of the trailer:

The manga by Hirohiro Araki began in 1987, while the Steel Ball Run part ran from 2004 to 2011. The full staff for the latest anime installment includes:

• Director: Yasuhiro Kimura & Hideya Takahashi (Golden Wind)

• Series Director: Toshiyuki Kato (Every Series)

• Series Structure: Yasuko Kobayashi (Every Series)

• Character Design: Daisuke Tsumagari (Golden Wind)

• Music: Yugo Kanno (Stardust Crusaders, Diamond is Unbreakable, Golden Wind, Stone Ocean)

• Sound Director: Yoshikazu Iwanami (Every Series)

• Animation: david production (Every Series)

A key visual for the 2nd STAGE was previously revealed.

title: TenSura Season 4 Cour 3 Set for July 2027, Clayman REVENGE Anime Announced for April
content:
That Time I Got Reincarnated as a Slime ( TenSura ) Season 4 will continue with its third cour in July 2027. In addition, the official spin-off That Time I Got Reincarnated as a Slime: Clayman REVENGE is getting a TV anime adaptation, set to begin in April 2027.

The announcements were made following the finale of Season 4’s second cour on September 25 through a collaboration video featuring Rimuru and Clayman. Season 4 was previously confirmed for five total cours .

Clayman REVENGE is based on a manga by Wataru Kajika, with the original story by Fuse. The spin-off follows Demon Lord Clayman after his ambitions are crushed by Rimuru, sending him 70 years into the past and exploring an alternate path his life might have taken.

Studio 8bit will handle animation production, as with the main That Time I Got Reincarnated as a Slime anime. Kentaro Sugimoto will direct, with Yuji Ikuhara on the series composition, and Asumi Hashimoto and Hideki Sakai as character designers. Takehito Koyasu will reprise his role as Clayman.

A teaser visual for Clayman REVENGE was also released.

Fuse shared the following comment:

“Clayman REVENGE started from a casual idea of mine, and now, incredibly, it’s getting an anime adaptation! Things have been moving forward smoothly ever since the project began, so even as the original creator who proposed it, I’m feeling pretty nervous about how quickly everything is progressing. (laughs) Clayman is scolding his subordinates with a serious expression, while the glass in his hand shakes and wine spills from it. It leaves a small stain on his pure white suit… and when Clayman notices, he desperately tries to cover it up so no one realizes how uncool he looks. The concept behind Clayman REVENGE was simply that this situation alone would already be funny. At first, I wrote the plot thinking it would be nice if it lasted around two volumes, but thankfully it has been well received by the fans, and now I feel like I want to continue it for as long as possible! While occasionally having Clayman act seriously, I want this to remain, at its core, a series people can simply enjoy. More than anything, I want not only Kajika-sensei and myself, but also everyone on the anime production staff, all the creators involved, to work together as one team and enjoy making the series. That is the spirit in which the Clayman REVENGE anime is being produced, so I would be very happy if you continue to support it!!”

Wataru Kajika also commented:

“Just being able to draw a That Time I Got Reincarnated as a Slime spin-off manga already felt like a miracle to me, so even after I was told it was getting an anime adaptation, it still didn’t feel real for quite a while! I’ve been shown the anime character designs and even had the chance to visit the recording studio, and I’ve just been constantly moved by everything…! I’m really, really looking forward to seeing Clayman’s army in the anime!!”

Fuse wrote the Tensura light novel series starting in 2014, featuring illustrations by Mitz Vah. The novel ended on November 29 last year with the release of Volume 23. The anime is adapting the manga, which is drawn by Taiki Kawakami.

The TV anime adaptation by studio 8bit began in October 2018, with the first season until March 2019. The second season was released through 2 split cours in Winter 2021 and Summer 2021. The third one began in April and concluded with Episode 24 on September 27, 2024.

That Time I Got Reincarnated as a Slime: The Movie – Scarlet Bond was the first movie for the franchise, and it premiered in 2022. The movie had an original story by the creator Fuse, also featuring the movie-original character called Hiiro.

Season 4 was announced alongside this second film after the conclusion of the third season. Crunchyroll is streaming both the first movie and three TV seasons. It’s also bringing the That Time I Got Reincarnated as a Slime the Movie: Tears of the Azure Sea ( Tensura Movie 2) to North America on May 1, 2026, with both Japanese with English subtitles and English dub screenings.
author: Anime Corner

title: Chizu Kamikō's Seijo Mellia to Sennen Ōkoku no Kishi Manga Ends
content:
Chizu Kamikō 's Seijo Mellia to Sennen Ōkoku no Kishi ( Saint Melia and Knight of the Millennial Kingdom ) manga ended on the KadoComi website on Friday.

The story follows Melia, a young girl unable to use magic who suffers at the hands of her new caretakers after being separated from her beloved grandmother. She has a fateful encounter with the princess's knight Douglas, who is in search of a mysterious cure for the princess's illness.

Kamikō launched the series on Kadokawa 's Young Ace Up web platform in 2021. Kadokawa shipped the sixth compiled book volume in June 2025.

Manga UP! publishes Kamikō's manga adaptation of Shusui Hazuki 's I'll Become an Elegant Villainess! ( Kareinaru Akujo ni Naritai wa! Aisare Tensei Shōjo wa, Tanoshii Nidome no Jinsei o Okurimasu ) light novel in English. Kamikō launched the manga adaptation on Square Enix 's Gangan Online web platform in March 2025.

J-Novel Club publishes Kamikō's My Death-Defying Dog: Man's Best Friend, World's Best Savior ( Uchi no Inu ga Tsuyosugirun Desu ga!? Tensei Shitara Megami-sama no Shukufuku de Sekai o Sukū Koto ni Narimashita ) manga in English.
author: ANN

title: Frieren Celebrates 3rd Anime Anniversary With Special Visual, Season 3 Still One Year Away
content:
Frieren: Beyond Journey’s End has revealed a special new visual to mark the third anniversary of the anime’s first broadcast in September 2023. The announcement was made during a special Season 2 screening event , attended by the main voice cast. Alongside the new visual, the official account also reminded fans that Season 3, which will cover the Golden Land Arc, is now just one year away from broadcast. Season 3 is set to release in October 2027.

The new anniversary artwork shows Frieren, Stark, and Fern celebrating with a “ridiculously huge hamburger,” with the original Hero Party reflected in the window. You can check it out below.

Kanehito Yamada writes the Frieren: Beyond Journey’s End manga, with illustrations from Tsukasa Abe. It has been serialized in Shogakukan’s Weekly Shonen Sunday manga magazine since April 2020. The manga is available to read via Sunday Webry, Viz Media, and the Shogakukan Comic website, while Crunchyroll streams the anime.

Studio MADHOUSE is in charge of the anime adaptation. The first season was directed by Keiichiro Saito, while Tomoya Kitagawa directed the second. The series composition was handled by Tomohiro Suzuki. Reiko Nagasawa was the character designer, with the chief animation direction led by Yuri Fujinaka, Reiko Nagasawa, and Maru Takase. Evan Call composed the music.

title: Katekyo Hitman Reborn! Anime Reveals Sixteenth and Final Ending Featuring "Canvas" by +Plus
content:
Katekyo Hitman REBORN! anime has officially released the creditless version of its sixteenth and final ending, featuring the song “Canvas” by +Plus. The song was used in Episodes 191-203, while the new video was released as part of the series’ 20th anniversary celebration.

The release follows yesterday’s release of the fifteenth ending, featuring the song “Famiglia” by D-51 . The releases are part of “REBORN! MUSIC MONTH,” a September-long music project celebrating the anime’s 20th anniversary. As previously reported, the campaign will have creditless versions of the series’ past theme song sequences released daily on the official YouTube channel.

These creditless sequences were previously included with physical releases of the anime but had not been officially made available online. You can watch the latest entry below.

The campaign began on September 1 with an official 25-song playlist featuring opening themes, ending themes and other music from the TV anime.

The manga by Akira Amano ran in Weekly Shonen Jump from May 2004 to November 2012, ending with a total of 42 compilation volumes. The series also received an anime adaptation, which ran for 203 episodes from October 7, 2006 to September 25, 2010. Studio Artland handled the production. The anime is available on Crunchyroll , who describe the story: Tsuna, a timid junior high student, is a failure at school, sports, and social life. But everything around Tsuna has been completely changed when a baby called Reborn, who claims to be an Italian hit man from Vongola family shows up! Reborn was sent to groom Tsuna for his future life as a mafia boss of the family!

But everything around Tsuna has been completely changed when a baby called Reborn, who claims to be an Italian hit man from Vongola family shows up! Reborn was sent to groom Tsuna for his future life as a mafia boss of the family!

title: Future GPX Cyber Formula's New Anime Short Reveals Cast, Staff, Screening on February 19
content:
Bandai Namco Filmworks announced on Saturday that its planned new anime short for the Future GPX Cyber Formula series will screen alongside a new HD remastered "movie edition" of the Future GPX Cyber Formula: Early Days Renewal compilation OVA in Japan starting on February 19, 2027. The new short anime is titled Shin Seiki GPX Cyber Formula ASURADA , and is a direct sequel to the 1998 Future GPX Cyber Formula Sin anime.

Character designer Hirokazu Hisayuki and chief mechanical animation director Satoshi Shigeta drew the below poster for the new anime short.

Series director Mitsuo Fukuda is overseeing the new "movie edition" of Future GPX Cyber Formula: Early Days Renewal .

The main staff for the new Shin Seiki GPX Cyber Formula ASURADA short includes:

• Planning, Production: Sunrise

• Original Work: Hajime Yatate

• Director: Scriptwriter: Mitsuo Fukuda

• Character Design: Hirokazu Hisayuki

• Cyber Machine Design: Shōji Kawamori

• Chief Mechanical Animation Director: Satoshi Shigeta

• Color Design: Ritsuko Utagawa

• Art Director: Yukiko Maruyama (Atelier Musa)

• Director of Photography: Kōsuke Nakanishi (Asahi Production)

• Editing: Yukiko Nojiri

• Sound Director: Sadayoshi Fujino

• Planning Cooperation: MegaHouse

• Production, Distribution: Bandai Namco Filmworks

The returning cast for the short includes:

• Jun-ichi Kanemaru as Hayato Kazami

• Kotono Mitsuishi as Asuka Sugo

• Toshihiko Seki as Bleed Kaga

• Yuri Amano as Kyōko Aoi

• Shūichi Ikeda as Kyoshiro Nagumo

According to the staff, the upcoming short uses hand-drawn animation and no CG.

Shōji Kawamori designed the previously revealed completely new Cyber Machine "Zenith Asurada AKF-S0/G" for the short. Bandai Namco Filmworks also revealed on Saturday Kawamori's design for the "Hō・Ōga AA-1" machine (name romanization not confirmed).

Additionally the company revealed four stills from the new anime short.

Bandai Entertainment released the Future GPX Cyber Formula anime as a complete collection on DVD in November 2003. The company described the story:

Cyber Formula is the future of Grand Prix auto racing where a mix of skilled driving and advance technology ultimately determines who wins and loses. Kazami Hayato is thrust into the fast paced world of Cyber Formula racing when he accidentally becomes imprinted to Team Sugo's Asurada GSX after recovering the racecar from would-be thieves. Now he must prove to himself and to his teammates that he can compete with the best racers in the world. Step into the world of Cyber Formula and prepare yourself for the fast lane.

The Future GPX Cyber Formula television anime aired in Japan in 1991. The anime had four OVA sequels: Future GPX Cyber Formula 11 beginning in 1992, Future GPX Cyber Formula Zero in 1994, Future GPX Cyber Formula Saga in 1996, and Future GPX Cyber Formula Sin in 1998. A compilation OVA titled Future GPX Cyber Formula: Early Days Renewal debuted in 1996.

The anime has inspired games that were originally created as fan works without copyright, but are now authorized and advertised on the official site.

A new game in the series is also in the works titled Future GPX Cyber Formula Spiral . The new racing game features an original storyline with supervision by the series' general director Mitsuo Fukuda .

title: The Fake Alchemist Reveals First PV and Key Production Details
content:
The production committee for The Fake Alchemist ( Nisemono no Renkinjutsushi )has released a promotional video and announced the anime’s cast and staff. Miyari Nemoto and Youhei Matsuoka will voice the leads, Nora and Paracelsus, respectively. Studio Passione, known for titles like Nukitashi the Animation and Interspecies Reviewers , will animate the series.

Takeo Takahashi, director of the original Spice and Wolf anime, will serve as chief director. The additional staff includes:

• Hijiri Sanapei — Director

• Kenta Ihara —Series Composition

• Luka Standridge — Composer

• Yuka Takashina — Character Designer

The anime’s premiere date and broadcasting details are unknown. Likewise, no Western streaming company has announced the anime’s acquisition.

You can watch the PV below:

Nisemono no Renkinjutsushi follows Paracelsus, who after his reincaranation now lives in the city-state of Orichalconia. Unlike the dull world he left behind, Paracelsus-kun’s new home is a fantasy realm filled with alchemy and magic. Yet even there, he’s only scraping by.

But Paracelsus’ life quickly begins to change when he buys a shaman slave-girl named Nora. That momentum builds when he tries to save Coco, an elf who’s lost her senses and limbs. After all, how could Paracelsus know that his attempt to help Coco ends with him fighting gods?

The anime adapts The Fake Alchemist, a manga written by Jiro Sugiura and illustrated by Umemaru. The manga is a remake of a webcomic Sugiura originally published on his Pixiv account. KadoComi and Nico Nico Seiga , both operated by Kadokawa, have serialized The Fake Alchemist since its June 2023 debut. Kadokawa has collected the chapters into five tankōbon volumes. Yen Press began publishing the English edition in August 2025.
